Opio Product Security Company Customers Book a demo CUSTOMER STORY Forvis Mazars Across markets and data rooms: how Forvis Mazars Group is scaling agentic AI Interviewed Pierre-Paul Jacquet Deal Advisory at Forvis Mazars Grégory Volpi Partner Transaction Services at Forvis Mazars Share this customer story Deployed across 10 countries, Opio is helping Forvis Mazars Group (“Forvis Mazars”) bring specialised, secure agentic AI into the everyday work of international transaction services teams. Transaction Services across borders Forvis Mazars Group, the international leader in audit and assurance, tax and advisory services, helps clients prepare for what’s next by combining international scale and reach with local market expertise. In Transaction Services, that means bringing together teams that understand the financial, operational and cultural realities of each market while maintaining consistently high standards and delivering seamless collaboration across an engagement. Grégory Volpi has more than twenty years of financial due diligence experience, including transactions across Europe, North America, Africa and Asia. Pierre-Paul Jacquet began his career in Paris and now advises on global transactions from his base in London. Having been involved in over 200 deals on the buy and sell side globally for corporates and investors, he also set up and led the Group's Financial Advisory practice across Asia-Pacific from Singapore. Their experience reflects a central reality of international transaction services: local environments vary, but clients expect the same support, quality and professional judgement wherever a transaction takes place. "London is one of the world's most international deal markets. Our teams need technology that can support the same standard of analysis across businesses, reporting environments and jurisdictions. Opio was built for that reality." PIERRE-PAUL JACQUET One specialised approach, across 10 countries Forvis Mazars has now deployed Opio across 10 countries, as a GenAI-powered solution to transform transaction advisory services and due diligence. This breadth demonstrates that the platform is not tied to a single jurisdiction, accounting environment or way of organising transaction services. Each market retains its local expertise and professional judgement, while teams share a specialised approach to bringing agentic AI into their work. For an international organisation, this matters. Innovation needs to travel across borders without imposing one country's operating model on another. A platform must be flexible enough to work within local requirements while maintaining a consistent level of quality, reviewability and control worldwide. The team worked with Forvis Mazars to ensure deep domain alignment, embedded controls and humanintheloop review capability – streamlining complex workflows while preserving professional judgment. This deployment, currently across 10 countries, gives Forvis Mazars a common foundation for adoption, while enabling each team to apply the technology to the realities and requirements of its own market and engagements. From experimentation to adoption Forvis Mazars views artificial intelligence as part of a broader transformation of professional services. The opportunity is not simply to provide teams with another tool. It is to embed new ways of working into the processes where technology can create meaningful value. Before adopting Opio more broadly, Forvis Mazars conducted a nine-month pilot to test the platform from end to end. The pilot assessed more than the quality of individual outputs. It examined how Opio fitted into Transaction Services team workflows, how professionals reviewed its work, how teams adopted it and how it could be deployed securely across the organisation. Opio worked alongside the Forvis Mazars’ AI team throughout this process. Transaction Services professionals identified the workflows that mattered. The AI team helped create the conditions for responsible adoption. Opio contributed technology and expertise focused specifically on the mechanics of the profession. Together, they helped teams learn how to frame work for specialised agents, provide the right context, review the supporting evidence and decide when an analysis needed to go further. "Adoption happens when the technology fits the reality of the engagement. Our work with Opio and our AI team is about helping people understand where agentic AI adds value, how to use it responsibly and how it can strengthen the quality of their work." GRÉGORY VOLPI Security as a foundation for scale Responsible AI and security was a core requirement defined by Forvis Mazars in the selection and deployment of Opio. It was considered from the beginning of the pilot, not added as a final technical review. Opio worked closely with Forvis Mazars IT teams to understand their requirements and prepare deployments adapted to the firm's infrastructure and governance standards. All outputs are subject to mandatory professional review, ensuring accountability, transparency and human oversight. The solution operates exclusively on secure client data rooms, does not train on client data and preserves strict confidentiality. Forvis Mazars wanted to ensure full traceability, with clear audit trails linking outputs to source documents. This ensured the essential compliance with data protection regulations, internal AI governance and professional standards, mitigating bias and operational risk by design rather than after deployment. Opio was also able to be deployed on premise, giving Forvis Mazars greater control of where sensitive information is processed and how the platform fits within its technology environment. This flexibility is critical for an international organisation. Local requirements may vary, but every deployment must provide the confidence required for teams to use the technology on live engagements. "Security was a major criterion from the start. Opio worked through our IT requirements and could support an on-premise deployment, giving us the confidence to move from a nine-month pilot to broader adoption." GRÉGORY VOLPI Why Forvis Mazars chose Opio Forvis Mazars was not looking for a general-purpose AI platform. It needed a specialist that understood Transaction Services, could operate across an international organisation and could meet the professional, IT and legal standards required for deployment. Opio's focus on the profession made that possible. Its team understood the workflows and level of scrutiny required on a live transaction. The platform passed the firm's business, IT and legal review, while its deployment model could be adapted to the security and infrastructure requirements of different countries. Deploying Opio across financial advisory engagements has streamlined transaction and accounting review workflows. Overall, this solution reduces manual document review, accelerates due diligence timelines and improves consistency across complex engagements. Its advisors can spend more time on professional judgment, risk assessment and client dialogue rather than data processing. Clients benefit from faster deal execution, clearer financial insights and an improved experience in timecritical transactions. The result is a solution designed not only to introduce agentic AI, but to make it usable, trusted and relevant in the everyday work of international deal teams. zh.summary: 围绕数据室、试算表、databook 与报告组织财务尽调 AI 工作流。
zh.judgment: 专业复核时间才是关键回报；减少整理不应增加交易判断错误。
zh.replaces: 交易团队整理数据室资料、对账与搭表，再重复写分析和尽调报告。
zh.product: 产品页将工作围绕一次真实尽调安排，提供预设流程并保留专业判断。安全和部署为公司披露，本次未接触客户数据室或生成报告。
zh.customer: 交易服务顾问与财务尽调团队是明确用户。项目时间压力和重复整理构成需求，买方应将采购费与交付工时、复核和责任一起评估。
zh.workflow: 用户接入数据室与财务资料，形成试算表及 databook，再在受控步骤中提出分析并由团队决定结论。异常数字与报告表述需要可追踪依据。
zh.business_model: 没有取得公开价目，机构或项目合同需确认。敏感资料接入、模板与方法适配可能增加前置成本；后续项目复用是经济上的关键。
zh.traction: 已核验 Forvis Mazars 的官方案例，描述跨国家采用；仍是公司和客户公开叙述。平均节省比例没有独立对照，不能当成所有项目的确定收益。
zh.moat: 专业方法、数据结构与机构审批习惯可能形成优势。普通文档助手、表格自动化与内部工具都是替代，真正区分在复杂项目的可复核结果。
zh.funding_read: 资本可支持企业交付，下一里程碑应是同机构后续项目及团队扩展。项目数量增长需扣除上线、复核与支持成本。
zh.risks: 错误账项或遗漏数据可能影响交易判断，跨地区口径与模板也不同。自动起草若增加专业审查负担，反而会抵消省下的整理工时。
zh.takeaway: 围绕一次专业交付组织数据、步骤与责任。把模型建议和最终判断分开，并让每个报告结果能回到原始数据。
zh.watch_next: 看可比项目整理和复核工时、数字纠错、报告修改及后续采用。用完整项目周期评价，而非仅计自动处理的文件数。

en.summary: Financial due-diligence workflows organized around datarooms, trial balances, databooks and reports.
en.judgment: Professional review time is the key return; less preparation must not create poorer transaction judgments.
en.replaces: Manually assembling dataroom information, reconciliations, analyses and reports.
en.product: The product page organizes a real engagement with predefined workflows and retained professional judgment. Security and deployment are company claims; no client dataroom was accessed.
en.customer: Transaction-services and diligence teams are stated users. Time pressure and repeated preparation create demand, assessed against review effort and delivery responsibility.
en.workflow: Dataroom and financial records feed trial balances and databooks; controlled steps suggest analysis while the team chooses conclusions. Exceptions and report statements need traceable evidence.
en.business_model: Public prices were not retrieved. Institution or project contracts need confirmation; sensitive-data setup and methodology adaptation create initial cost. Reuse on later engagements matters.
en.traction: An official Forvis Mazars story describes adoption across countries. It remains vendor/customer testimony; average savings without an independent comparison cannot guarantee every project’s return.
en.moat: Methodology, data structures and approvals could create advantages. Document assistants, spreadsheets and internal tooling compete on complex, reviewable results.
en.funding_read: Capital supports institutional delivery. Later projects and team expansion are milestones, after accounting for setup, review and support.
en.risks: Wrong accounts or omitted data affect judgments; regional conventions differ. Drafting that creates more professional checking can offset preparation savings.
en.takeaway: Organize data, steps and ownership around one professional deliverable. Separate model suggestions from decisions and trace reports to source data.
en.watch_next: Watch preparation, review, corrections, report changes and repeat use on comparable engagements. Evaluate the whole cycle rather than processed-file counts.
